excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
Regarding block delay, we’ve looked into this a fair bit over the past 6 months or so. We haven’t been able to attribute it to a single client, but we’ve been able to attribute it to pools a bunch of times. We’ve reached out to all of them and most of them have done something to fix it.

We’ve spent a while optimising in LH for fast block proposals and propagation and I don’t think it’s all that hard to achieve decent times. I think the other clients are fast too, from what I can tell. I suspect it’s mostly pools with fancy infrastructure who aren’t aware that they’re underperforming.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: I certainly think it’s worthwhile trying to fingerprint late producers and applying pressure to whoever is causing the delay. These late blocks are already a pain and it’s only going to get worse.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<sigpaul> One of the things we did was to add scary logs whenever we (a) produce a block and publish it late and (b) when we take too long to forward a block. 
I think it’s worthwhile other clients doing this too. Then, users might be more aware if their fancy infrastructure is slowing things down.

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: the `kintsugi` branch does its CPU selection a little differently -- normally, Nimbus uses `-march=native`, so indeed would avoid `SIGILL`. But that branch uses `-march=broadwell`, because it's the earliest CPU which gets some substantial speed improvements for BLS operations, instead

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: generally, it's been a decent balance between allowing people to build docker images or other portable executables without worrying about march=native creating issues taking a build from a 2 year old machine to a 4 year old machine or similar, but it doesn't currently try to detect whether Broadwell is available. If not, then one has to use something like `-d:disableMarchNative` to force it back to SSSE3 (nearly universal)
